message.content:
**Columbia University** Columbia University is an Ivy League research university located in New York City, United States. It was founded in 1754 as King's College by royal charter of King George II of Great Britain, making it the fifth-oldest institution of higher education in the United States. In 1784, after the American Revolution, the college was renamed Columbia College, and later became Columbia University in 1896. Key facts: | Item | Details | |------|---------| | **Location** | Morningside Heights, Manhattan, New York City (main campus), with additional campuses in Morningside Park, Upper Manhattan, and the Columbia Business School in Midtown Manhattan. | | **Founding year** | 1754 (as King's College) | | **Type** | Private research university | | **Ivy League member** | Yes | | **Student population** | Approximately 30,000 students (undergraduate, graduate, and professional). | | **Academic structure** | • Columbia College (undergraduate liberal arts)
• Graduate School of Arts & Sciences
• Fu Foundation School of Engineering and Applied Science
• School of Journalism
• School of Social Work
• School of Public Health
• School of Law
• School of Medicine
• School of Architecture, Planning and Preservation
• School of International and Public Affairs
• Columbia Business School | | **Notable alumni** | • Barack Obama (former U.S. President) – attended Columbia Law School
• Alexander Hamilton (founding father) – studied at Columbia College
• Ruth Bader Ginsburg (Supreme Court Justice) – attended Columbia Law School
• J.D. Salinger (author) – attended Columbia College
• Many Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and other distinguished scholars across disciplines. | | **Research focus** | Columbia is known for its interdisciplinary research across fields such as medicine, engineering, social sciences, humanities, and environmental science. It hosts several research centers and institutes, including the Columbia Climate Institute, the Center for Data Science, and the Columbia Center for Oral Health Research. | | **Campus features** | • Low Memorial Library (iconic central library)
• Butler Library (largest library on campus)
• Morningside Park (open green space)
• The historic Low Memorial Library’s reading room is a popular spot for students and visitors. | | **Athletics** | Columbia Lions compete in NCAA Division I as part of the Ivy League. The university has a strong tradition in rowing, tennis, and track & field. | Columbia University is renowned for its rigorous academic programs, distinguished faculty, and vibrant intellectual community. Its location in New York City provides students with access to cultural institutions, internships, and global networking opportunities.
